problem: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{x+3}+\frac{1}{x-3})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.

examples.knowledge_point: Integrating a Combination of Linear Rational Functions Using the General Formula
examples.worked_solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{1+2x}+\frac{1}{1-2x})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{1+2x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{1-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+2x|-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-2x|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{1+2x}{1-2x}|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|\frac{1+2x}{1-2x}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.

feedback.problem: Calculate $\int \frac{1}{3x+4}\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let $u=3x+4.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{3x+4}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+4|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the above by writing $C=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ for another arbitrary constant $K,$ and then we can combine the two terms using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+4|+C & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+4|+\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+4|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|3x+4|)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we finally conclude that

$$
\int \frac{1}{3x+4}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|3x+4|).
$$
